correctness.rationale: For the smooth construction of the cited very general (1,6)-polarized abelian surface, the headline Hodge table and polarized factor are correct. The family has (q,p_g,c2)=(4,6,12), so b2=26. Grossi–Moretti describe a finite map from the nine-point blow-up to P² and its smooth cubic Galois closure. The finite first projection has degree two and factors through the transposition quotient; the resulting finite birational map to the normal blow-up is an isomorphism. The nine centers are one free translation orbit, so passing to K gives the one-point blow-up of A/K. The full finite quotient is P²/K. Rational cohomology of these quotients gives invariant cohomology, compatibly with Hodge structures. Crucially, a module a·1+b·sign+c·V is already determined by its dimension a+b+2c and its invariant dimensions a and a+c under S3 and a transposition. Thus (26,1,7) gives (1,13,6) on H² and (6,0,1) gives (0,4,1) on H²,⁰ without using any A3 thesis input. Theorem 5.6 gives H¹,⁰=2V. Conjugation, duality and subtraction give the whole table; the character values at a transposition and a three-cycle are -12 and 8. For the polarization, average an ample class, making the standard isotype primitive. Its invariant cup-product pairing factors through a positive invariant form on V by absolute irreducibility; Hodge–Riemann gives signature (2,4) on the six-dimensional multiplicity space. The frozen checker verifies its arithmetic inputs and implications, not its cited geometry; it was read, not run. The table implies the stated A3 invariant dimensions and Euler trace 18 but does not itself establish the local fixed-point types; the thesis passage for those ancillary attributions remains unverified. No realization by a K3 surface is implied.
